- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly.  
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (sentiment < 0.3) or shows strong downward momentum.  
- Overreact to short-term sentiment swings; model lags sentiment shifts by 1–2 days, especially when sentiment turns sharply.  
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds prices too high in strong bullish sentiment and too low in strong bearish sentiment, failing to reflect intermediate-term equilibrium.  
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive, then underestimate later periods (last 10–15 days) when sentiment turns neutral or negative.  
- Avoid “sentiment echo” — model amplifies sentiment trends without adjusting for structural price constraints (e.g., floor near 60–65).
